observations: body L1-L10: the figure stands at the left of lines 1 to 10, which are set beside it in a narrow measure. It is redrawn from measurements of the print: the meridian as a circle with a short mark at the zenith; the horizon and the equator as diameters; the axis from the centre to the pole in dashes, each dash where it printed; the double arcs marking the equal angles of the horizon and the equator on either side of the centre; the braces φ and alt. merid. along the circle; the italic words Zenith (reading upward), Polus, horizon and aequator, the sign of Aries, and alt. merid. and meridianus set along the circle.

body L1: rule (α) is right: the meridian altitude of a star is 90° − φ ± δ, the declination added when it is northern and subtracted when it is southern. For the equator (δ = 0) it is 90° − φ, as the figure shows: the arc φ from the horizon to the pole, the quadrant from the pole to the equator and the arc alt. merid. from the equator to the horizon make up the half circle above the horizon.
body L6: the dash of «al–Battānī» is a long dash (5.3 pt).

body L7: rule (β) is rule (α) of chapter 16 (p. 190) and is right: with R = 1 and H the meridian altitude, 1 − cos P = 1 + tg φ tg δ = sin H/(cos φ cos δ) and sin h = sin φ sin δ + cos φ cos δ cos t give (1 − cos P)(1 − sin h/sin H) = 1 − cos t. The minus sign is printed as a long dash (9.7 pt); it is set as a minus sign.
body L11: in «differentia» the t is broken away; only a trace of it printed.
body L17, L22: the heads of the notes on chapters 22 and 24, «Ad» and «caput» in small capitals, in the larger type of the heads.
body L18, L23: in the heads, the dashes after «a)» measure 9.8 pt each and the dash of «35–36» 5.4 pt; transcribed as dashes and a long dash.

body L21: rule (α) is rule (β) of L7 solved for sin h, and is right: sin vers t = sin vers P (1 − sin h/sin alt. merid.) gives sin h = sin alt. merid. (sin vers P − sin vers t)/sin vers P. The minus sign is printed as a long dash (10.0 pt); it is set as a minus sign.

body L28-L31: rule (α) is right: the meridian altitude of the first point of Aries is 90° − φ (L1), so its sine is cos φ, and the second form, sin δ = cos φ sin amplit./R, is the rule of chapter 7, sin amplit. = R sin δ/cos φ, solved for sin δ.
body L29: «[meridiana]» stands in square brackets in the print.
body L33: the rules are those of chapter 19 (p. 195): P = 90° ± the ascensional difference, the sign + for a northern declination, and sin differ. ascens. = R tg φ tg δ.
notes L1: the dash of «1-2» measures 3.4 pt, as a hyphen.
